A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AFLOW paper with 38 readable pages, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–38 are identical; changes are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, transfer and cost analyses, a GSM8K operator ablation, and human/LLM evaluations of novel and academic-idea generation in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix F's human/LLM evaluation results in Tables A1–A2.

M1.justification: The code-represented workflows, operators, MCTS selection/expansion/evaluation/backpropagation procedure, and Appendix F's open-ended-task adaptation are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval, MBPP, MATH, GSM8K, HotpotQA and DROP, plus novel generation and academic-idea generation in Appendix F. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains IO, CoT, CoT SC, MedPrompt, MultiPersona, Self Refine and ADAS. The cross-model comparisons and Appendix F's direct-LLM comparisons also remain identical.

E3.justification: The validation/test splits, dataset sampling, model configurations, temperatures, optimization budgets and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix F also retains the same generation and human-evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The GSM8K operator ablation, cross-model transfer analysis, workflow case studies and optimization traces are identical in Section 5.2 and Appendices B–C. Appendix F's open-ended case studies are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose the same split seed, five validation executions with mean and standard deviation, and three-run averaging for Tables 1–2. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, costs, rankings and qualitative findings are identical throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables A1–A2. For example, Table 1's AFLOW average remains 80.3.

T1.justification: The workflow/search-space definitions, selection equation and Appendix G's assumptions and arguments about completeness, convergence and search efficiency are unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims about workflow optimization, MCTS-based automation, benchmark superiority and cost efficiency retain the same meaning and scope. The abstract's code-availability update does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of transferability, operator benefits, execution feedback and cost efficiency are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same discussion of tasks lacking numerical feedback and the use of LLM-based evaluation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise to release code upon publication with a statement that code is available at the FoundationAgents/AFlow GitHub repository. This adds concrete access information; implementation details and appendix code listings are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix E, the bibliography and comparisons with prior research are identical. No cited works or research-positioning arguments are added or removed.

P1.justification: The abstract's final code-availability sentence is rewritten and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other prose and the section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 1 has localized abstract reflow around the new repository link and an updated arXiv stamp. All figures, tables, captions and rendered layouts on pages 2–38 are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 replaces a future code-release promise with a specific repository pointer, modestly improving code discoverability and reproducibility guidance. The scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
